key_insight: A native 2D pairwise quantum-circuit ansatz can be more expressive and less prone to trainability issues than comparable 1D entanglement designs at shallow depths.
engineering_relevance: For planar superconducting-qubit hardware, matching the ansatz to the device connectivity can improve early-stage variational performance without needing deeper circuits.
method: Built a 2D pairwise PQC aligned with native planar connectivity.
Compared against representative 1D chain/ring ansatze at the same layer depth on 16 qubits.
Evaluated expressibility with KL divergence and second-order frame potential, and trainability via gradient variance of a global Pauli-Z string.
evidence_signal: On the 16-qubit benchmark, the 2D ansatz shows the lowest KL divergence at L=1 and L=2, faster convergence of the frame potential toward its lower bound, and smaller gradient variance for L=1–4 before the differences diminish by L=6.
watch_item: The reported advantage is strongest at shallow depths and for a specific observable, so results may not generalize to all costs, qubit counts, or hardware noise conditions.
paper_title: Expressibility and trainability of a two-dimensional pairwise quantum-circuit ansatz
